coverage_notes:
SOURCES USED. (1) Wikipedia, "2022 Georgia Bulldogs football team" — its "Coaching staff" table, the roster-footer coaching box, and the "Football support staff" / "Graduate assistants" / "Analysts" bullet lists. (2) The georgiadogs.com staff directory archived on the Wayback Machine at https://web.archive.org/web/20220803015505/https://georgiadogs.com/staff-directory, which contains a 69-person "Football" category plus a 4-person "Strength and Conditioning - Football" category. Together these yield 78 documented people.

SNAPSHOT-DATE CAVEAT. I queried the Wayback CDX index for georgiadogs.com/staff-directory over 2022-2024 and the only captures are 20220205, 20220307, 20220405, 20220614, 20220707, 20220802/20220803, then nothing until 20240520 (a 308 redirect). There is NO archived athletics-site staff directory from December 2022 or January 2023. The directory rows therefore reflect the roster as of Aug 2-3, 2022 (preseason of the 2022 season), not the Jan 9, 2023 championship game date. Personnel who joined the program after August 2022 would not appear, and I have no way to detect them from this source.

WIKIPEDIA/ARCHIVE DISCREPANCIES (lower confidence rows). Five people appear on Wikipedia's 2022 support-staff or graduate-assistant lists but are absent from the Aug 2022 archived directory: Eric Black, Maurice Sims, Meaghan Turcotte, Garrett Murphy, Rashawn Scott. They may be post-August-2022 hires, or Wikipedia's list may be partly drawn from a different season. In two cases the archived directory shows a different person in what looks like the same job (Mitch Bernardo as "Director of Football Creative Video" vs. Wikipedia's Eric Black; Cate Herrmans as "Assistant Director of Football Nutrition" vs. Wikipedia's Meaghan Turcotte). I kept all five because each has a real Wikipedia citation, but they should be treated as the weakest rows in this set.

Also note Wikipedia's "Coaching staff" table is footnoted to the *2021* Georgia Bulldogs Football Media Guide, not the 2022 guide. The roles in it are nonetheless 2022-correct (Will Muschamp, Stacy Searels, Fran Brown, Bryan McClendon and Chidera Uzo-Diribe all shown in their 1st season), and every on-field coach in it is independently confirmed by the Aug 2022 archived athletics-site directory, so I treated it as reliable for 2022.

ROLE-WORDING CONFLICTS. Wikipedia and the athletics site word several jobs differently. Examples: Matt Godwin is "Player personnel coordinator" on Wikipedia but "Director of Player Personnel" on the athletics site; Angela Kirkpatrick is "On-campus recruiting coordinator" vs. "Associate Director of Recruiting Operations"; Logen Reed is "Assistant recruiting coordinator" vs. "Associate Director of Recruiting Operations"; Neyland Raper is "Assistant director of football operations & recruiting" in Wikipedia's support-staff list but "Director, Football Operations" in Wikipedia's own roster-footer box and "Director of Football Operations" on the athletics site; Anna Courson is "Assistant, Football Operations" vs. "Football Operations & Travel Coordinator". Where they conflict I recorded one source's wording in the role field and cited both.

ANALYST vs. QUALITY CONTROL. The athletics site gives everyone in this tier a "Quality Control - Offense/Defense/Special Teams" title, while Wikipedia separately lists six of them under an "Analysts" heading. I used role_category "analyst" for those six (Bobo, Benedict, Faulkner, Merritt, Rob Muschamp, VanGorder) and "qc" for QC-titled staff not on that list, and "gradasst" for the four on Wikipedia's graduate-assistant list plus the two the athletics site titles "Graduate Assistant - Defense". This split is a judgment call — in this era the two labels describe the same non-countable staff tier.

MID-SEASON DEPARTURE. Buster Faulkner was hired as Georgia Tech's offensive coordinator in December 2022, before the Jan 9, 2023 title game; his Wikipedia article nonetheless states he won two national championships in his three years at Georgia. Flagged with a midseason_note.

WHAT I COULD NOT DOCUMENT. (a) Medical/athletic-training staff: the archived directory's "Athletic Training/Sports Medicine" category (Ron Courson, Anna Randa, and roughly 20 trainers) is department-wide and contains no sport assignments, so I could not establish which of them were the football staff. Rather than guess, I included NO athletic-training rows. This is a real gap — a football champion certainly had assigned trainers. (b) The 2022 Georgia football media guide: I could not retrieve it; Wikipedia's own citation is to the 2021 edition. (c) Scott Cochran is widely reported to have been on medical leave during the 2022 season while treated for cancer; I could not verify this with a citation and have listed him at his titled role with no midseason_note. (d) My web-search budget was exhausted at the start of this task (200/200 calls already used by the session), so I could not run contemporary-news searches for hire/departure announcements and had to work from direct URL fetches only. That means mid-season arrivals and departures other than Faulkner are likely undetected. (e) WebFetch is blocked from web.archive.org in this environment; I retrieved the archived directory via curl, so quotes attributed to the Wayback URL were verified against the raw archived HTML.

QUOTE-MATCHING NOTES. Wikipedia quotes are taken from the article wikitext (https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=2022_Georgia_Bulldogs_football_team&action=raw) and are given in their rendered plain-text form (link brackets and italic markers removed), which is how they appear to a reader. One quote, Eric Black's, contains a literal non-breaking space (U+00A0) immediately after the first en dash — that is genuinely what the page contains and is preserved verbatim. Wayback quotes are the exact staff-title cell text; on that page the person's name sits in an adjacent table cell of the same row, and each row's link carries an aria-label combining both, which I reproduce in the note field.
